narrative: OMX30 opens with tailwinds from overnight US performance and risk-on commodity moves, though technicals flash overbought signals requiring caution. Gold's 1.44% surge and copper strength (+1.22%) provide direct support to Boliden and mining exposure. USD/SEK at 9.515 (+0.66%) remains constructive for Volvo, Atlas Copco, and Ericsson exporters. The index sits 8.7% above its 200-day moving average in confirmed bull territory, but Stochastic overs at 81.8 and RSI at 52.86 (neutral-to-firm) combined with ADX weakness at 8.4 suggest mean-reversion risk if momentum falters. Yields down (-0.13% on 10Y) marginally pressures banking NIM expansion, partially offsetting commodity gains.
morningBrief: OMX30 expected to gap higher on US NASDAQ momentum and risk-on sentiment, targeting +0.4% open. Watch 3180 (50-MA) as near-term resistance; support holds 3085 (lower Bollinger). Commodity strength drives sector rotation: LONG Boliden on gold/copper, WATCH Atlas Copco and Volvo B (USD/SEK strength) for export re-rating. Banks (SEB A, Handelsbanken A) sideways as yield compression offsets equity relief — avoid early enthusiasm. Ericsson B and Hexagon B track NASDAQ closely; gains capped by tech sentiment. Stochastic at 81.8 warns against chasing highs; scale into longs on any morning dip toward 3123. US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET is key afternoon trigger. ADX below 18 reduces trend conviction — treat moves as tactical rather than structural.
